cluster.title: Hierarchical Cluster Analysis
cluster.weightIgnored: CLUSTER ignores case weights: WEIGHT is in effect, but every case counts once.
cluster.noIcicle: Icicle plots are not available; use /PLOT=DENDROGRAM for a dendrogram.
cluster.tooMany: {{n}} cases are too many for hierarchical clustering (at most {{max}}; memory and time grow with the square of the number of cases). Select fewer cases, or use QUICK CLUSTER (k-means).
cluster.tooFew: At least two cases with valid values are needed for clustering.
cluster.proximityLarge: The proximity matrix is shown for at most {{max}} cases.
cluster.dendrogramLarge: The dendrogram is drawn for at most {{max}} cases.
cluster.moreThanCases: Solutions with more clusters than the {{n}} cases are skipped.
cluster.badRange: {{what}} expects (n) or (min, max) with whole numbers 1 ≤ min ≤ max.
cluster.noMatrix: /MATRIX (matrix input) is not supported; cluster the cases of the active dataset.
cluster.noVars: A list of numeric variables is required.
cluster.badMeasure: Unknown measure “{{token}}”. Use SEUCLID, EUCLID, COSINE, PEARSON, CHEBYCHEV, BLOCK, MINKOWSKI(p) or POWER(p,r).
cluster.badPower: MINKOWSKI(p) and POWER(p,r) need positive numbers.
cluster.badMethod: Unknown method “{{token}}”. Use BAVERAGE, WAVERAGE, SINGLE, COMPLETE, CENTROID, MEDIAN or WARD.
cluster.pearsonVars: MEASURE=PEARSON correlates cases across variables and needs at least two variables.

hierCluster.title: Hierarchical Cluster Analysis
hierCluster.saveMembership: Save cluster membership as new variables
hierCluster.icicleInfo: Icicle plots are not available; the dendrogram shows the same merges.
hierCluster.standardizeInfo: Values are used as they are. If the variables use very different scales, standardise them first (Descriptives → Save standardized values) and cluster the Z-scores.
hierCluster.errRange: The minimum number of clusters must not exceed the maximum.
hierCluster.errPearson: Pearson correlation between cases needs at least two variables.
hierCluster.hintSeuclid: Centroid, median and Ward's method are meant for squared Euclidean distances.
